handoff: review#3 approve: the detached norn check-run fixes the cause (tick no longer blocks; heartbeat, claim renewal, K3 rerun, timeout→fail, status '(check running)' with age all work). Typecheck + 1220 tests green. Only minor findings: claimRunLease false ignored (F1), lease stuck if identify fails and check-run dies before claiming (F2), command orphaned when check-run is killed (F3), person commands don't stop a running check (F4), silent catches/sweep before try (F5), run_id not ULID-validated (F6); nits F7-F8.

findings.title: runCheckOrder ignores claimRunLease's false
findings.detail:
When the lease is gone or names another run by the time check-run starts, check-run still runs the command and writes a receipt. This needs the starting tick to have failed to identify the child, then exited, and then K3 to reclaim the lease, all within check-run's startup. The result is a second run with no lease, against K1.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: When the claim returns false, exit without running anything, writing a receipt or releasing the lease.

findings.title: Lease stuck when identify fails and check-run dies before claiming it
findings.detail:
With `norn watch`, a failed identify leaves the lease held by the long-lived watch pid. If check-run then dies before claimRunLease (for example, a missing order makes it refuse), the lease never goes dead, so the unit shows check.running forever.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: When identify fails, hand the lease over to {pid, start unknown} or stamp it with a short deadline. Alternatively, have check-run release the tick-held lease when it refuses.

findings.title: Check command orphaned when check-run is killed
findings.detail:
runShell starts the command in its own process group, and only check-run enforces the timeout. If check-run is SIGKILLed or OOM-killed, the command keeps running with no timeout. K3 then starts a second copy in the same worktree and on the same ports. Before this change, a killed tick had the same exposure.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Record the command's pgid in the lease or order so that K3 reclaim kills it, or run the command in check-run's own group.

findings.title: Person commands do not stop a running check-run
findings.detail:
`norn release`, `drop` or `workflow --to` can now run while a check is in progress. check-run carries on and writes a stale receipt into runs/, possibly in a worktree that has been removed.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Have person commands that leave the step kill the check lease holder, or have check-run skip the receipt when the unit's run_id no longer matches.

findings.title: Silent catches in the sweep and in identify
findings.detail:
`catch { return; }` in sweepCheckOrders swallows every error, not only ENOENT, so an EACCES hides orphan orders for good. `identify(...).catch(() => null)` leaves no trace when the probe fails. Separately, sweepCheckOrders runs before the try block, so if it throws, the tick's lease leaks until K3 reclaims it.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Catch only ENOENT, record a failed probe, and move the sweep inside the try block (or before acquireRunLease).

findings.title: run_id positional not validated as a ULID
findings.detail:
The run_id goes straight into checkOrderPath, so `../x` resolves outside ~/.norn/checks. Schema validation of the order limits the damage.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Reject anything that is not a ULID (ids.ts) before reading the order.

findings.title: Layering and duplication
findings.detail:
The order-directory listing and unlink policy (sweepCheckOrders) live in cli rather than store. claimRunLease and releaseRunLease share the same read/validate/match prefix. CheckOrder sits in schema claim.ts.
Axis: standards

findings.title: Wall-clock assertion and internal-call tests
findings.detail:
`duration_ms < 2500` may flake under CI load; asserting that the tick returns before the receipt exists would be more robust. Two tests call runCheckOrder directly rather than `norn check-run`. The zombie.ts test-helper fix is unrelated to #77; mention it in the PR.
Axis: spec
